stories.headline: Connecticut’s Secretary of the State was one of the targets of the suspicious powder letters sent to election offices nationwide
stories.summary: Connecticut’s Secretary of the State says her Hartford office was the intended target of one of the suspicious letters the FBI and U.S. Postal Inspection Service are investigating around the country. Federal authorities intercepted the Connecticut letter before it arrived. Some of the mailings to election offices held a powdery substance, but preliminary tests in several states found nothing hazardous. Election offices in Louisiana and Oklahoma were evacuated Tuesday after workers opened envelopes with white powder. Before learning Connecticut had been targeted, the office reminded town election officials of safe mail-handling procedures. “I’m relieved that the substances tested so far have not been hazardous, but these incidents are still deplorable,” Secretary Stephanie Thomas said. “No one should have to fear for their safety simply because they’re doing their jobs.” Thomas also joined the National Association of Secretaries of State and the state election directors’ group in a joint statement condemning the mailings. Her office says it remains in close contact with the FBI and other law enforcement agencies, less than three weeks before Election Day.

stories.headline: Jets activate rookie WR Omar Cooper Jr. off injured reserve and elevate LB Jaden Keller for Sunday at New England
stories.summary: The Jets moved first-round rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. from injured reserve to the 53-man roster Saturday, so he will play Sunday against the Patriots in Foxborough. They also elevated linebacker Jaden Keller from the practice squad. Cooper hurt his ankle in the Week 1 win over Tennessee after only five snaps. One of those snaps was a 30-yard catch-and-run that set up the opening-drive touchdown. He has missed the four games since. Sunday will be only his second NFL game. He had 69 catches for 937 yards and 13 touchdowns at Indiana last season. Keller, an undrafted rookie from Virginia Tech, has played 38 special-teams snaps over the last two games. Sunday will be his third straight game for the Jets. He had 10 tackles in the preseason after joining the practice squad Aug. 31.

stories.headline: Former U.S. ambassador Morse Tan is stuck in South Korea and on trial for defamation over a speech he gave in Washington
stories.summary: Morse Tan, who served as ambassador-at-large for global criminal justice in President Trump’s first term, appeared in a Seoul court Friday on criminal defamation charges brought on behalf of South Korean President Lee Jae Myung. The case stems from a June 2025 talk at the National Press Club in Washington on alleged fraud in South Korea’s presidential election. Answering a question there, Tan repeated old allegations that Lee was involved in a violent crime as a teenager and spent time in juvenile detention. South Korean prosecutors say those claims are false. A second charge covers remarks Tan made in South Korea in July 2025. He has been barred from leaving the country since he arrived in May. Tan is a constitutional-law professor and former dean of Liberty University’s law school. He pleaded not guilty, calls the case “political lawfare” and says criminal defamation “does not exist in the U.S.” South Korea’s embassy says the case follows due process. The State Department declined to discuss specifics. Tan could face prison if convicted.

stories.headline: TikTok permanently bans the account for Alex Gibney’s “Musk” documentary, citing political-policy violations
stories.summary: TikTok has permanently suspended the promotional account for “Musk,” Alex Gibney’s unflattering documentary about Elon Musk, which runs three hours and 52 minutes. According to The Hollywood Reporter, distributor Bleecker Street was told Friday that the ban was coming because of the “level of severity with political-policy violations,” and that “some violations trigger immediate suspension.” TikTok has not said which rule the account broke. The film opened nationwide Friday after a limited preview. Last month YouTube, Meta, X and TikTok all turned down ads for it. Google and Meta later reversed course, calling it an error, but TikTok and X did not. X has also refused to take Bleecker Street ads for its other films. Gizmodo points out that Oracle, controlled by Larry Ellison, owns about 15% of the consortium that runs TikTok’s U.S. business, and Ellison’s ties to Musk come up in the film. Gizmodo also notes that political content is everywhere on TikTok, and that the platform’s special rules for “political accounts” cover governments, politicians and parties, not films.

stories.headline: Nearly 12-foot alligator drags a 71-year-old fisherman into a Florida pond and kills him
stories.summary: A 71-year-old man fishing at a park in Winter Garden, Florida, was pulled into the water and killed by a nearly 12-foot alligator Friday evening, according to the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission. Wildlife officials identified him as Steve Hamilton. The attack happened around 5 p.m. at Dr. Bradford Memorial Park, west of Orlando. The park has several small ponds that connect to Lake Apopka and is so well known for alligators that it has a crossing called Gator Bridge. Police said Hamilton was standing on shore when the alligator grabbed him. Trappers removed an 11-foot, 8-inch alligator from the scene. “Lake Apopka has tons of alligators in it,” Winter Garden Police Capt. Michael Mason said. “It looks like it’s docile… but it can be dangerous.” Hamilton is the second person killed by an alligator in Florida this year. Florida usually sees about a dozen attacks a year, and the FWC has counted 32 fatal attacks since 1948, never more than three in a single year.

stories.headline: Al Jourgensen says Ministry “has run its course” as the final album lands Oct. 30 and a goodbye tour hits 2027
stories.summary: Ministry founder Al Jourgensen says the industrial-metal band is done after one last album and farewell tour. “I just think that Ministry has run its course,” he told Hit Parader. “I’m glad it was here when it was here.” Ministry’s 17th and final studio album, “Hate To Go (Take Out Or Delivery),” comes out Oct. 30 on Cleopatra Records. Jourgensen, 68, called it “a culmination of 40 years of the same elements” and “a good one to go out on.” He said he is “not enthused about continuing to keep doing this kind of music or music in general.” Jourgensen says he only ever wanted to teach history and that Ministry “kept dragging me in,” comparing himself to Michael Corleone in “The Godfather Part III.” The album closes with “We’re Still Here,” a final collaboration with former member Paul Barker. The “Goodbye Europe” tour with Die Krupps starts in April 2027, and a full U.S. run follows. Ministry started in Chicago in 1981 and hit its peak with “The Land Of Rape And Honey,” “The Mind Is A Terrible Thing To Taste” and 1992’s Grammy-nominated “Psalm 69.”

stories.headline: A new Canon patent includes an RF 70-200mm f/2L IS design, a full stop faster than any 70-200 Canon sells
stories.summary: A Japanese patent application from Canon (JP 2026-168807) contains about a dozen optical designs for fast zooms, and one of them is an RF 70-200mm f/2L IS. That would be a full stop brighter than Canon’s f/2.8 versions and a natural partner for the RF 28-70mm f/2L. Canon Rumors says the design uses 23 elements in 8 groups, including 6 aspheric surfaces, and appears to zoom and focus internally. Its optical length is about 220mm before adding the flange distance. The EF 200mm f/2L prime was 210mm long as a complete lens. The patent’s real focus is a three-group focusing system. One main group does most of the work, and two lighter groups move only slightly to correct field curvature, which keeps the motors small and the lens compact. Other designs in the filing include zooms faster than f/2, such as a 50-85mm f/1.4. Canon Rumors cautions that patents often never become products. It says there is “a very small chance” a 70-200 f/2 reaches stores and guesses one would cost $6,000 to $8,000.

stories.headline: Trump says there’s “zero chance” he replaces Susie Wiles and calls the Politico report a “fake story”
stories.summary: President Trump shot down reports that he has been thinking about replacing White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles. Politico’s Playbook newsletter reported Thursday that Trump had been asking allies what they think of Wiles and “musing about replacements,” possibly Deputy Chief of Staff for Policy Stephen Miller. Speaking to reporters Friday, Trump said there was “zero chance” of that. “The Susie Wiles story was a fake story. She’s been incredible,” he said, adding that the administration has had “maybe the most successful two years” in presidential history. He called Wiles “smart” and “tough” and noted that she “just went through a lot with the cancer surgery” and has fully recovered. Trump announced her breast cancer diagnosis in March, and Wiles said in September that she was cancer-free. Trump said the White House had told Politico before publication that the story was “totally wrong.” He added, “The only one that matters is me, because I’m the one that makes the decision,” and said Wiles is “gonna be here for a long time.”

stories.headline: Pope Leo XIV walks out of Gemelli Hospital and returns to the Vatican four days after lung cancer surgery
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV left Rome’s Gemelli Hospital Saturday afternoon and went back to the Vatican, sooner than expected after Tuesday’s surgery. His doctors said blood tests and a chest X-ray that morning showed he was well enough to go home. Video showed the 71-year-old walking out on his own and waving to well-wishers. Before leaving he celebrated Mass in a room on the hospital’s 10th floor. He is expected to lead Sunday’s Angelus prayer from the window of the papal apartment. The Vatican says recovery should take about a week, and his public schedule is cleared until at least Oct. 20. During the 90-minute, minimally invasive operation, surgeons removed the lower lobe of his right lung, more than the “localized nodule” first announced. Tests confirmed lung adenocarcinoma, the most common type of lung cancer, including in nonsmokers. Outside doctors told NPR that choosing surgery first suggests the cancer was caught early. Leo is still scheduled to visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru in early November.

stories.headline: Three men get more than 158 years each for murdering two Australian surfers and their American friend in Baja
stories.summary: A Mexican judge on Friday sentenced three men to 158 years and nine months in prison each for killing Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson, 30 and 33, and their American friend Carter Rhoad, 30. The three were camping on a surfing trip near Ensenada, Baja California, in April 2024 when they were shot in the head during an attempted robbery. Their bodies were found days later in a cliff-top well. Judge Raul Hernandez ruled that the defendants, named only as Jesus Gerardo, Irineo Francisco and Angel Jesus, acted with premeditation. Jesus Gerardo, known as “el Kekas,” already had a criminal record. Prosecutors say the killers saw the group’s pickup and tents and wanted the truck’s tires and parts, then burned the tents and the truck to destroy evidence. His former girlfriend, who admitted pushing him to steal the tires, got 20 years last November. The judge turned down prosecutors’ request for more than $100,000 in damages and said the families would have to sue for that in civil court. “There can never be justice for the loss of a son, but we are grateful that these men will never hurt anyone else,” Rhoad’s mother said.

stories.headline: Tesla’s new Roadster reservation contract says it “cannot guarantee” when — or if — buyers will get a car
stories.summary: Two days after Tesla showed off its next-generation Roadster, buyers are reading the fine print. InsideEVs spotted it first, and The Drive reports that the reservation agreement on Tesla’s site says the car “is still under development and so we cannot guarantee when your vehicle will actually be delivered or if it will be delivered.” Tesla is again asking for up to $250,000 up front, the same as for the first-generation Roadster, which took deposits nearly 10 years ago and never reached production. A reservation buys only an “approximate” place in line, not a confirmed build slot. Price, options, features and hardware could all change before customers are invited to configure their cars. Tesla currently estimates production will start in 2028. There is some good news: reservations are fully refundable, and unlike the Cybertruck Foundation Series, there is no no-resale clause, though reservations can’t be transferred. That matters, given Musk’s promises of 0–60 mph in 0.81 seconds and built-in thrusters.

stories.headline: Cody Wilson unveils the WASP, a 3D-printed pistol designed by “GatGPT,” which he calls an AI that can generate guns
stories.summary: Cody Wilson, the gun-rights activist behind Defense Distributed and the first 3D-printed gun, the Liberator, has unveiled what he calls “the first AI-made gun.” The weapon, called the WASP, was first reported by The Verge. It was designed through a conversation with GatGPT, a custom AI model trained on the gun-file library of DEFCAD, Defense Distributed’s online repository, which can also help builders choose parts. Wilson stresses that he hasn’t just made one AI-designed gun but “an AI that can generate guns.” The WASP is a single-shot, Liberator-style design, basically a pistol barrel attached to a spring-loaded plastic box. It fires real bullets and has no serial number. Experts The Verge spoke with pointed out some odd features: an unfinished trigger guard that leaves the trigger exposed, and a grip that looks inverted. Wilson calls firearm access “a fundamental human right.” He predicts that back-and-forth between users and AI could sharply speed up new 3D-printed designs. Mainstream chatbots refuse to help with this, while states and courts are still fighting over how to regulate homemade guns and parts kits.

stories.headline: Adrian Smith: Iron Maiden is enjoying playing live “as much, if not more than ever” 50 years in
stories.summary: Iron Maiden guitarist Adrian Smith says the band is still having a blast more than 50 years after Steve Harris founded it in 1975. “We’re still together, we’re still friends, and we’ve had our ups and downs,” he told Peru’s Radio Oxigeno. “I think we’re enjoying playing live as much, if not more than ever,” he added, with “more younger fans, new blood” in the crowd. The “Run For Your Lives” world tour plays a classic-era setlist from the first nine albums, from the 1980 debut through 1992’s Fear Of The Dark. The show opens with “Murders In The Rue Morgue” from Killers and includes first-album songs he didn’t play on. Relearning them was “like riding a bike… It’s in the brain, in the muscle memory,” he said. Smith, who joined in 1980, said he feels “physically better than I probably did in my 20s,” but the band now paces its schedule. His advice to his 24-year-old self: “It’s only rock and roll. Don’t take it so seriously,” though he admits being hard on himself is probably why he’s still doing it.

stories.headline: Stellantis workers in Canada vote this weekend on a strike mandate, with talks stalled over the Brampton plant sale
stories.summary: Unifor members at Stellantis in Canada are voting Saturday and Sunday on whether to authorize a strike, and results are due Monday, Oct. 19. A yes vote would let the bargaining team call a walkout if needed. Talks opened Sept. 1 and broke off Sept. 11, and the old contract expired Sept. 20. Unifor wants wages and benefits that match its recent deals with Ford and GM, plus clear product commitments for its plants. The union says Stellantis has tied the core money terms to an agreement to close and sell the idled Brampton, Ontario, assembly plant. Stellantis has signed a memorandum of understanding with Canadian armored-vehicle maker Roshel about a possible sale. About 2,200 Brampton workers are on indefinite layoff since the plant stopped in 2023, and Stellantis pulled its next-generation Jeep Compass from the site in 2025, moving it to Illinois. A strike could hit Windsor Assembly, which builds the Dodge Charger and Chrysler minivans. Windsor’s third shift and future work at Etobicoke Casting are also sticking points. Stellantis says it is still willing to negotiate a deal.

stories.headline: Trump waives the Graham Act’s Russia sanctions and 100% tariffs on Russian-oil buyers two days before they kicked in
stories.summary: President Trump signed an executive order late Friday waiving key parts of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia Act, the bipartisan law he signed last month. Starting Sunday it would have put 100% tariffs on the five biggest importers of Russian crude and natural gas, a group that includes China, India and Turkey. Trump also waived the law’s 500% tariffs on Russian goods and paused some other sanctions. He used a provision that lets the president certify to Congress that a waiver is “in the national interests of the United States.” The waivers stay in place until officials decide more action is needed, and agencies are told to keep watching countries that buy Russian energy or dodge sanctions. The move follows last week’s easing on Russian diesel, part of Trump’s push to bring down energy prices that spiked during the Iran war. Putin envoy Kirill Dmitriev called it “truly historic.” Zelenskyy called it “unfortunate” and a “sanctions blackout” that rewards Putin. A bipartisan group of senators had already called the diesel waivers a “betrayal” of Ukraine.

stories.headline: Penguins blow a 2-0 lead as the Avalanche score five straight in a 5-2 loss; Chinakhov has no timeline to return
stories.summary: The Penguins (3-4-1) had their best period in weeks in Denver Friday night. They outshot Colorado 14-5 in the first, and Evgeni Malkin and Bryan Rust scored 29 seconds apart for a 2-0 lead. Then the Avalanche (5-2-1) scored five unanswered goals at Ball Arena. Artturi Lehkonen scored twice, including the tying goal 25 seconds into the second, off a Kaedan Korczak giveaway behind the net. Gabriel Landeskog got a free tap-in, rookie T.J. Hughes scored his first NHL goal, and Nathan MacKinnon added a power-play one-timer, finishing with a goal and three assists. Arturs Silovs stopped MacKinnon on a penalty shot and made 27 saves. Pittsburgh went 0-for-3 on the power play and is now scoreless on its last 20 chances. One bright spot: Sidney Crosby’s assist moved him past Joe Thornton for seventh on the NHL’s all-time assists list, with 1,110. Forward Egor Chinakhov (lower body) missed the game, has no timeline to return and is expected to miss tonight’s game at Vegas and Monday’s at Utah.

stories.headline: St. Joseph girls soccer stays unbeaten, beating Greenwich 3-1 in Trumbull’s No. 1 vs. No. 2 FCIAC showdown
stories.summary: Trumbull’s St. Joseph High School won Friday’s top-ranked girls soccer matchup on its home field. The Cadets beat No. 2 Greenwich 3-1 and handed the Cardinals their first loss of the season. The win keeps St. Joseph unbeaten heading into the end of the regular season and in prime position for the upcoming FCIAC tournament, where Greenwich could get a rematch. Saturday’s Trumbull Patch AM also notes a celebration of life for longtime Connecticut musician Darik Pearson, frontman of Darik and the Funbags. It runs Sunday, Oct. 18, at Abriola Parkview Funeral Home on White Plains Road in Trumbull. Voters are reminded that the Nov. 3 general election is coming up, with early voting starting Monday.

stories.headline: Judge lets Alex Murdaugh’s defense run a ‘high risk’ DNA test that could use up the last samples from Maggie’s phone and fingernails
stories.summary: At a pretrial hearing in Lexington, South Carolina, on Friday, Judge Debra McCaslin sided with Alex Murdaugh’s lawyers over prosecutors’ objections. She allowed new DNA testing on swabs from Maggie Murdaugh’s cellphone and on clippings from under her fingernails, even though the testing will likely use up the last usable material. McCaslin said due process requires “a meaningful opportunity to present a full and complete defense.” The defense says all three samples contain unidentified male DNA. It wants the lab Othram to run a Y-STR test, which isolates the Y chromosome, to see whether a single unknown man is the source. Lead prosecutor Creighton Waters called the test “high risk” and said even the defense’s own expert expected little, adding that Othram’s first quantification came back as “goose eggs on the Y chromosome.” Murdaugh was convicted in 2023 of murdering his wife Maggie and son Paul. The South Carolina Supreme Court threw out the verdict because former clerk of court Becky Hill had improperly influenced the jury. His retrial starts April 5, 2027.

stories.headline: Apple rewrites App Store rules to go after AI deepfakes, ‘nudify’ apps and bait-and-switch features added after review
stories.summary: Apple on Friday expanded its App Review Guidelines to cover AI-generated nonconsensual intimate imagery. Explicit content was already banned, but the updated rule 1.2 now names AI content-creation apps and requires developers to actively prevent and remove AI deepfakes, or risk being pulled from the App Store. MacRumors notes the rule could apply to apps like xAI’s Grok. Earlier this year Apple threatened to remove Grok over nude deepfakes, and xAI added safeguards before an update was approved. A new guideline, 2.5.19, targets “bait-and-switch” apps that hide features during review and switch them on later, a trick Apple ties to “nudification” apps that make explicit images of real people. Developers caught doing it risk removal from both the App Store and the Apple Developer Program. Apple also extended its ban on apps that facilitate human trafficking or child exploitation to alternative app marketplaces. “We do not hesitate to remove apps, and terminate the developers behind them,” Apple said.

stories.headline: Santa Ana winds drive the Norte Fire through coastal San Clemente and San Juan Capistrano; 16,000 ordered out
stories.summary: A fast-moving fire pushed by dry Santa Ana winds burned at least six homes in Southern California on Friday, engulfing expensive coastal properties in Orange County. The Norte Fire started in San Clemente and was blown into San Juan Capistrano, where firefighters fought blazing homes next to tennis courts and pools under black smoke visible for miles. By Friday night about 16,000 residents were under evacuation orders, the Orange County Fire Authority said. Two firefighters were hospitalized with heat-related injuries, nine schools closed, and the cause is not yet known. The fire was under a square mile as of Friday evening. A separate fire near Camp Pendleton shut part of Interstate 5 for hours, and tens of thousands of Californians had their power cut as a precaution. Fire-weather conditions and a coastal heat advisory last through Saturday night. “Had these winds been a little bit stronger, a little bit different direction, this could have been a whole lot worse,” San Clemente Mayor Rick Loeffler said.
